statement: Meta plans to put its third-generation custom MTIA 450 silicon into data centers in the first half of 2027 and a fourth-generation MTIA 500 in late 2027, explicitly to reduce dependence on Nvidia hardware.
why: A top-five buyer moving inference and training work onto in-house accelerators shifts spend away from merchant GPUs toward custom silicon and its design and foundry partners.

impact.mechanism: Custom processors designed with Broadcom and built at TSMC substitute for merchant GPU purchases in Meta's fleet, lowering Meta's operating cost while diverting a share of accelerator demand.

evidence.excerpt: The company intends to introduce custom processors into data centers during early 2027, aiming to reduce dependency on Nvidia hardware and lower operational expenses.
an initial batch of 12 test units arrived September 1 from TSMC, with performance metrics within 2-3% of design projections

confidence.basis: Secondary outlet summarising Bloomberg reporting; single publisher, no primary filing, and deployment is still at test-unit stage.
